sections.overview: Umbrina cirrosa is a coastal sciaenid fish of the eastern Atlantic, Mediterranean and Black Sea region.
sections.identification: A short, firm barbel beneath the chin and oblique yellowish flank lines help distinguish it from the brown meagre.
sections.habitat: It lives in coastal water over rocky, sandy or gravelly bottoms, and juveniles often enter estuaries.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on fish and bottom-dwelling invertebrates, and also takes algae.
sections.behavior: It is generally described as sedentary and close to the coast.
sections.reproduction: Spawning occurs in spring and summer.
sections.ecology: It is a coastal food fish and is caught by both commercial and recreational fisheries.
sections.conservation: An Italian assessment cites a Mediterranean IUCN listing of Vulnerable from 2013 and identifies overfishing and habitat alteration as concerns.
